# A clear way to review your short-form videos
Free sample from the Shortform Review Kit by Project ZERO.

## Before leaving notes
Open the version named in the editor's message. Watch the entire clip once. Then replay it and record changes. Ask one person to combine team feedback so the editor receives a single set of decisions.

## Use this format
Clip ID: [C01]
Version: [v01]
Timecode: [00:08–00:11]
What needs to change: [describe the issue]
Requested result: [specific replacement or outcome]
Priority: [required / preference / question]
Approved by: [decision maker]

## Turn vague feedback into an editable request
Instead of: “Make it more exciting.”
Try: “C01 v01, 00:00–00:03: start with the close-up product shot and remove the greeting. Keep the voiceover after that.”

Instead of: “The text is wrong.”
Try: “C02 v01, 00:12: replace ‘everyday’ with ‘every day’. Use this spelling in the caption file too.”

Instead of: “Can you make another version?”
Try: “We need an extra square version of C03 for a separate placement. Please confirm the added work and timing before starting.”

## Resolve conflicts before submitting
If one reviewer wants a longer introduction and another wants it removed, ask the final approver to choose. Keep unresolved questions in the notes, clearly marked as questions.

## Close the round
Send one consolidated list. When you approve, name the exact clip IDs and versions. Silence does not mean approval. New footage, a new concept or an additional format may require a separate scope decision with your editor.
